subject: AI & Agents
title: AlexNet and the GPU Breakthrough
description: Learn AlexNet and the GPU Breakthrough in one minute.

hook.text: In 2012, two grad students used gaming hardware to demolish an AI competition. Nobody saw it coming.

buildup.text: Alex Krizhevsky and Ilya Sutskever trained a deep neural network on NVIDIA GPUs.

discovery.text: GPUs — designed for video game graphics — turned out to be perfect for parallel matrix math.

twist.text: Their model cut the ImageNet error rate nearly in half. The gap was unprecedented.

climax.text: The AI world pivoted overnight. Deep learning went from niche to mainstream in months.

punchline.text: Video game chips accidentally launched the AI revolution.

quiz.question: Why were GPUs important for deep learning?
options: They excel at parallel math operations neural networks need
They were the cheapest available hardware
They were specifically designed for AI

details.summary: AlexNet's 2012 ImageNet victory proved that deep neural networks trained on GPUs could crush traditional computer vision. It cut error rates nearly in half and launched the deep learning revolution.
details.whyItMatters: AlexNet demonstrated that depth plus GPU compute equals unprecedented performance. This insight redirected the entire AI field toward deep learning and GPU-based training within months.
takeaways: AlexNet cut ImageNet error rates from 26% to 16% in 2012
GPU training made deep neural networks computationally feasible
The result redirected all of AI research toward deep learning

faq.question: What made AlexNet different from previous approaches?
faq.answer: It used a deeper neural network than competitors and trained on GPUs, which were much faster than CPUs for parallel matrix operations. It also used dropout and ReLU activation, which improved training stability.

faq.question: How quickly did the field shift after AlexNet?
faq.answer: Within one to two years, nearly every top ImageNet competitor switched to deep learning. GPU companies like NVIDIA saw their AI business explode, and deep learning became the dominant AI paradigm.
